Evidence-backed application screenshots

01 — Executive summary

The Concourse server-backed application passed its current automated suite. BRAD/BMAD orchestration remains partially validated: native TEA could not be invoked, 85 route scenarios were not behaviorally executed, stakeholder collaboration and matched comparisons were not run, and AC-02/AC-04 remain blocked.

02 — Application demonstration

The demo provides SQLite-backed projects and stories, role-gated HTTP actions, version conflict handling, review/QA evidence, defect retests, audit history and release readiness. See the verified screenshots and setup instructions.

03 — Full SDLC execution

The current evidence covers implementation validation and a previously recorded live delivery journey. It does not establish a complete independent PM→BA→Architect→developer→QA→release chain through BRAD.

04 — Stakeholder performance

Ten roles are defined; no role-specific independent BRAD requests or native workflow outcomes were measured. Seeded demo accounts are fixtures, not stakeholders.

05 — BRAD routing evaluation

All 85 canonical catalog records passed static metadata/hash checks. L2, L3, L4 and L5 remain NOT_RUN for all 85; no behavioral accuracy percentage is reported.

06 — Native BMAD invocation

No native BMM, Architect, Build, code-review or TEA workflow was verified in this current host. The TEA probe was blocked because the host loader did not discover the workflow.

07 — Developer collaboration

Three independent Concourse developers and two QA stakeholders did not execute. A separate installer-test candidate worktree and one read-only review context are recorded separately and are not counted as the requested collaboration study.

08 — QA and TEA evaluation

The app passed 27 server, 15 web unit, 40 quality, 3 delivery integration and 27 browser tests. A separate reviewer found a specification conflict. Native TEA and manual assistive-technology review remain unrun.

09 — Ticket lifecycle analytics

The documented app journey exercised role-separated local delivery and defect retesting; no BRAD ticket-to-PR lifecycle or remote delivery is claimed.

10 — Reliability and recovery

BRAD v0.4.1 Node tests reproduced two test-harness failures. Candidate-only tests reportedly pass after portability/parser changes. Task interruption/resumption and duplicate-PR experiments were not run.

11 — Installer and host compatibility

Observed baseline is Windows 11, Node 24.19.0, npm 12.0.2. The package dry-run and repository/release checks pass; cross-version and other-host compatibility were not tested.

12 — BRAD versus direct BMAD

No matched tasks were run; sample size is zero. There is no measured speedup, quality delta, or cost comparison.

13 — Performance analytics

Only test-runner durations available in tool output are included. Model requests, tokens, cost, and complete workflow timing were unavailable and are left null.

14 — Failure analysis

The register separates confirmed test-harness defects, acceptance specification gaps, and host capability blockers. No host blocker is attributed to BRAD without evidence.

15 — BRAD v0.5.0 changes

Prioritize npm pack output normalization and Windows link-test portability as candidate test-harness improvements; separately improve host capability reporting only after a reproducible BRAD runtime issue is established.

16 — Production readiness

Not ready for a supervised team pilot or production. Application verification is local and the key orchestration, collaboration, authorization-oracle, and remote-delivery gates remain incomplete.

17 — Roadmap to v1.0

Repeat the evaluation on an authorized brownfield project, complete host-native invocation and independent collaboration experiments, and set quantitative gates before measuring outcomes.

18 — Reproducibility and evidence appendix

The versioned run contains the manifest, tests, 85-case results, event ledger, analytics, findings, hashes, machine-readable data, and validator. No PR, CI, publication, merge, or deployment occurred.

Findings and root-cause register

P1/P2 values are project finding priorities, not security vulnerability severities. Host capability and acceptance-specification blockers are not attributed to a BRAD runtime defect without evidence.

FindingPriority / statusComponentExpected / observedRoot cause / impactConfidenceEvidence
F-TEST-WIN-SYMLINKP2 · CONFIRMEDBRAD Windows Node test suiteExpected: The linked-target protection test reaches BRAD logic on Windows.
Observed: Directory symlink creation fails with EPERM before BRAD is invoked.		Root cause: The test requires Windows symlink privilege instead of a privilege-free junction.
Impact: Windows CI cannot run the safety regression in the current privilege environment.		96%E-BRAD-NODE, E-BRAD-CANDIDATE
F-TEST-NPM-PACK-SHAPEP2 · CONFIRMEDBRAD distribution content testExpected: The test parses supported npm pack JSON and asserts required package files.
Observed: The test indexes the result as an array; npm 12.0.2 returned an object keyed by package name.		Root cause: Test harness assumes one npm output shape.
Impact: A valid package is reported as a failed test on the observed npm version.		99%E-BRAD-NODE, E-BRAD-PACK, E-BRAD-CANDIDATE
F-ACCEPTANCE-PERMISSION-MATRIXP1 · CONFIRMED_GAPConcourse role authorization acceptanceExpected: An approved role/action matrix defines every forbidden role/action pair.
Observed: Selected role denials are implemented/tested but the approved matrix does not exist.		Root cause: Missing product/QA acceptance decision; not evidence of an authorization implementation defect.
Impact: AC-02 and exhaustive A04 conformance cannot be judged.		100%E-ACCEPTANCE-GAPS, E-APP-SERVER
F-ACCEPTANCE-MISSING-CRITERIAP1 · SPECIFICATION_CONFLICTConcourse acceptance-criteria creation contractExpected: An owner-approved oracle defines omitted and empty acceptance criteria at create time.
Observed: Both forms returned 201 and persisted an empty list in Draft; API contract suggests the field is required, while AC-04 says required-vs-optional is unspecified.		Root cause: Conflicting contract language; owner interpretation is absent.
Impact: AC-04 cannot be marked pass/fail; downstream requirement review is blocked.		100%E-AC04-PROBE, E-ACCEPTANCE-GAPS, E-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW
F-NATIVE-TEA-DISCOVERYP1 · BLOCKEDCopilot native TEA workflow discoveryExpected: A host-discovered installed TEA skill is invoked and leaves verifiable evidence.
Observed: TEA instructions were only in an external cache; workspace `_bmad` and host skill registration were absent; the native loader reported not found.		Root cause: Current workspace/host capability boundary; BRAD runtime defect is not established.
Impact: Native TEA execution and L4 routing evaluation remain unverified.		98%E-NATIVE-TEA
F-INDEPENDENT-COLLABP1 · NOT_RUNMulti-stakeholder execution evidenceExpected: Three independent developer worktrees and two independent QA stakeholder contexts collaborate through real handoffs.
Observed: No such stakeholder collaboration was executed; one separate read-only review context and one separate installer-candidate worktree were used.		Root cause: Evaluation scope not completed; no defect attribution to BRAD.
Impact: Role usability, coordination, and three-developer dependency claims remain unmeasured.		100%E-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, E-BRAD-CANDIDATE
